In this exercise, we'll link **manual decision-tree reasoning** to how a **random forest** works.

A decision tree is a flow-chart–like model that makes predictions by asking a series of yes/no questions about the data, splitting it into smaller and smaller groups until each branch mostly contains one class.

Each group (A–F) has a different subset of features and examples. We will:

1. Make a manual decision tree using your group's dataset (mammal vs. not mammal)
2. Train one decision tree using your group's dataset
3. Train a decision tree and a random forest on the full dataset
4. Compare and discuss

**Package note:** The random forest uses the `ranger` package. If you do not already have it installed, run the following command once in the R console:

```r
install.packages("ranger")
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3learners)
library(data.table)
library(rpart.plot)
```

Download your group's `.csv` file and `animal_traits_full.csv` from D2L → Content → Datasets → AnimalDecisions and place them in the same folder as this file.

## Part 2: Train your group's decision tree

Load your group's dataset. Replace `???` with your group's letter (A–F).

```{r load-group}
group_data <- read_csv("animal_traits_set_???.csv")
```

Convert the text columns to factors and remove the `Animal` column, since the animal's name should not be used to predict its class.

```{r prepare-group}
group_data_train <- group_data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
  select(-Animal)
```

Now train a decision tree to classify all of the animal classes (Bird, Crustacean, Mollusk, Mammal, Amphibian, Fish, Reptile).

```{r group-tree}
task <- TaskClassif$new(
  id = "tree",
  backend = as.data.table(group_data_train),
  target = "Class"
)

learner <- lrn("classif.rpart", predict_type = "response", minsplit = 1)
learner$train(task)

rpart.plot(learner$model, type = 0, extra = 102,
           main = "Group Decision Tree")
```

## Part 3: Load the full dataset

```{r load-full}
full <- read_csv("animal_traits_full.csv") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

full %>% glimpse()
```

### Train/test split

We'll randomly use 70% of the data for training and hold out 30% for testing.

```{r split-data}
set.seed(42)
n <- nrow(full)
train_ids <- sample(seq_len(n), size = 0.7 * n)
train_animals <- full$Animal[train_ids]
test_ids <- setdiff(seq_len(n), train_ids)
test_animals <- full$Animal[test_ids]

data_full <- full %>% select(-Animal)
```

---

## Part 4: Decision tree vs. random forest

### Decision tree on the full data

```{r full-tree}
task_full <- TaskClassif$new(
  id = "animal_full",
  backend = as.data.table(data_full),
  target = "Class"
)

tree <- lrn("classif.rpart", predict_type = "response", minsplit = 1)

# Train only on training rows
tree$train(task_full, row_ids = train_ids)

# Predict on held-out test rows
pred_tree <- tree$predict(task_full, row_ids = test_ids)

acc_tree <- pred_tree$score(msr("classif.acc"))
cat("Decision tree accuracy on test data:", round(acc_tree, 3), "\n")

rpart.plot(tree$model, type = 0, extra = 102,
           main = "Decision Tree (Full Data)")
```

### Random forest on the full data

```{r full-forest}
set.seed(42)
forest <- lrn("classif.ranger", predict_type = "response",
              num.trees = 300, importance = "impurity")

# Train only on training rows
forest$train(task_full, row_ids = train_ids)

# Predict on held-out test rows
pred_forest <- forest$predict(task_full, row_ids = test_ids)

acc_forest <- pred_forest$score(msr("classif.acc"))
cat("Random forest accuracy on test data:", round(acc_forest, 3), "\n")
```

```{r compare}
cat("Decision tree:", round(acc_tree, 3),
    "| Random forest:", round(acc_forest, 3), "\n")
```

## Part 5: Feature importance

```{r importance}
importance <- forest$model$variable.importance %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE)
importance_df <- tibble(Feature = names(importance),
                        Importance = as.numeric(importance))

importance_df %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Feature, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#228B22") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Feature Importance (Random Forest)",
       x = NULL, y = "Importance Score") +
  theme_minimal()
```
